newsitem.title: USA: Record cold in U.S. Midwest damages fruit.
newsitem.headline: Record cold in U.S. Midwest damages fruit.

text.p: Record-breaking cold temperatures Wednesday in the Midwest may have damaged budding fruit crops, meteorologists said.
Low-temperature records were set from the upper Midwest to southern Ohio and Kentucky, catching many fruit trees in bloom and vulnerable to the cold, Weather Services Corp.'s Peter Leavitt said.

At Hidden Valley Fruit Farm near Cincinnati, workers were inspecting the 60-acre orchard for signs that several varieties of apples, cherries, peaches, plums and pears suffered in the 15-degree weather.
"The peaches were blooming and some of the apples were starting," said an employee at the farm who declined to be named. "The cherries were blooming. You got one shot, they don't bloom again."
Indianapolis set an all-time record low for the month of April of 18 degrees, and Springfield, Ill., set a record of 19 degrees.
